api_server_tab.host_tooltip:
IP address the API server will listen on.
Use 127.0.0.1 for local-only access, or 0.0.0.0 to allow external connections.
api_server_tab.port_tooltip:
Port number the API server will listen on.
Default: 8000. Must be between 1-65535.
Make sure this port is not already in use by another application.
api_server_tab.workers_tooltip:
Number of worker processes for the API server.
More workers can handle more concurrent requests but use more memory.
Recommended: 1 for single-user, 2-4 for multi-user scenarios.
api_server_tab.max_concurrent_scans_tooltip:
Maximum concurrent scan operations per worker.
Limits CPU contention when multiple requests arrive simultaneously.

Effective system limit = workers × max_concurrent_scans.
Set to 0 to disable limiting (default).

Recommended: workers=2, max_concurrent_scans=2 for 6-core systems.
api_server_tab.cors_tooltip:
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) allowed origins in JSON format.

Use ["*"] to allow all origins (less secure but convenient).
Use ["http://localhost:3000", "http://example.com"] to restrict to specific origins.

Only needed if accessing the API from a web browser.
api_server_tab.memory_tooltip:
Enable memory usage monitoring for scan operations.

When enabled, memory usage statistics will be logged for each scan.
Useful for diagnosing memory issues, but adds slight overhead.
api_server_tab.auto_trim_tooltip:
Automatically release unused memory after each scan completes.

Helps prevent memory accumulation during long-running sessions.
Recommended: Enabled (may cause brief pauses after scans on some systems).
api_server_tab.web_icon_mod_tooltip:
Mod to use for item icons in the web interface.

When the web interface displays scan results, icons will be loaded
from this mod. If an icon is not found in the specified mod,
it will fall back to 'vanilla'.

Available mods depend on what you've imported into the database.
api_server_tab.no_auth_tooltip: API server will accept requests from anyone without authentication.
api_server_tab.basic_auth_tooltip:
Require username and password for API access.
Credentials are sent with each request in the Authorization header.
api_server_tab.bearer_auth_tooltip:
Require a bearer token for API access.
Token is sent in the Authorization header with each request.
api_server_tab.token_tooltip:
Secret token required for API authentication.
This token should be kept secure and sent in the Authorization header.

scanner_tab.database_path_tooltip:
Path to the template database file containing item icons for recognition.

This is a required HDF5 (.h5) file that must be generated before scanning.
Use the 'generate-templates' command to create this file.
scanner_tab.cache_size_tooltip:
Number of template resolutions to keep in memory for faster matching.

Maximum: 16 (total number of supported resolutions).
Setting higher than 16 has no effect.
Recommended: 0, 1, or 2 for low-memory servers.
scanner_tab.early_exit_tooltip:
Confidence threshold to stop searching early when a good match is found.

Value between 0.0-1.0. Set to 0.0 to disable (always check all templates).
Recommended: 0.99x (0.990-0.999) for speed, or 0.0 for accuracy.
Intermediate values can cause false detections for some items.
scanner_tab.confidence_gap_tooltip:
Controls when alternative matches are included in JSON output as candidates.

All items with confidence within this gap from the best match are included.
Set to 0.0 to disable candidates (only include best match).

Recommended: 0.1 (typically results in few items with alternatives per stockpile).
At 0.2, about half the items will have candidates.
scanner_tab.screenshots_folder_tooltip:
Optional folder to automatically save processed screenshots.

When set, scanned images are saved to daily subfolders (YYYY-MM-DD)
with format: Date_Time_StorageType_Name_Resolution.png

Leave empty to disable screenshot archiving.
scanner_tab.debug_mode_tooltip:
Save debug images showing the detection process.

Saves to current directory:
- stockpile_detection_result.png - Original image with detection boxes
- stockpile_quantities_result.png - Composite quantities image
- stockpile_name_region.png - Extracted name region
- stockpile_type_region.png - Extracted type region
- stockpile_shard.png - Extracted shard region

Useful for troubleshooting detection issues.
scanner_tab.extract_icons_tooltip:
Save each detected item icon as a separate image file.

Icons are saved to './icons/' folder with format: 'XXX_CODE.png'
where XXX is the icon index (000, 001, etc.) and CODE is the detected item.

Development setting - useful for creating new templates or debugging detection.

output_tab.description:
Configure output handlers for scan results.
You can add multiple handlers to send results to different destinations.
output_tab.move_up_tooltip: Move selected handler up in priority
output_tab.move_down_tooltip: Move selected handler down in priority
output_tab.order_info: Handler order matters: The first handler that returns a response (return or webhook) will have its data passed back to the client.

handler_dialog.name_tooltip: A friendly name to identify this output handler
handler_dialog.handler_type_tooltip:
Where to send scan results:

• return - Return data to caller (API mode)
• file - Save to a file
• webhook - POST to a webhook URL
• console - Print to console output
handler_dialog.output_format_tooltip:
Format for the output data:

• json - Full JSON with all stockpile data
• csv - Comma-separated values (one row per item)
• tsv - Tab-separated values (one row per item)
handler_dialog.file_path_tooltip:
Path where scan results will be saved.

Supported placeholders:
  {timestamp} - Full timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS)
  {year}, {month}, {day} - Date components
  {hour}, {minute}, {second} - Time components
  {stockpile_type} - Type (Seaport, Storage Depot, etc.)
  {stockpile_name} - Name of the stockpile
  {resolution} - Screen resolution (e.g., 1920x1080)

Example: {timestamp}_{stockpile_type}_{stockpile_name}_{resolution}.json
handler_dialog.webhook_url_tooltip:
URL to POST scan results to.

Results will be sent as JSON in the request body.
The webhook should accept POST requests with application/json content type.
handler_dialog.auth_type_tooltip:
Authentication type for webhook requests:

• null - No authentication
• basic - HTTP Basic Auth (username:password)
• bearer - Bearer token in Authorization header
• forward - Forward client's Authorization header to webhook
handler_dialog.auth_token_tooltip:
Authentication credentials for webhook.

• For basic auth: use format 'username:password'
• For bearer auth: just the token value

Required when auth type is 'basic' or 'bearer'.
handler_dialog.client_auth_tooltip:
Name of the Authorization header to forward from API client to webhook.

Useful when the webhook needs to know who initiated the scan.

Required when auth type is 'forward'.
handler_dialog.row_format_tooltip:
Row output format, comma separated

Available parameters:
 timestamp - last update timestamp, expressed as number of seconds since 1/1/1970
 timestamp_datetime - last update timestamp, expressed in a human-readable format
 structure_type - code name of structure in which the current item is located in 
 region - stockpile region code name 
 structure_x - normalized structure x coordinate 
 structure_y - normalized structure y coordinate 
 stockpile_name - reserve stockpile name, this parameter will be "Public" if the item is not in a reserve stockpile
 item_code_name - code name of current item
 item_display_name - display name of current item
 item_quantity - quantity of current item 
 item_crated - TRUE if current item is crated, FALSE otherwise
 NONE - empty column, use for padding

notifications_tab.description:
Configure Discord webhooks to receive notifications about stockpile scans
and server events. You can add multiple notifiers with different settings.
notifications_tab.enable_tooltip: Master switch to enable or disable all notifications

notifier_dialog.name_tooltip: A friendly name to identify this notifier
notifier_dialog.webhook_tooltip: Discord webhook URL for sending notifications
notifier_dialog.username_tooltip: Custom username shown for webhook messages
notifier_dialog.events_description: Select which events should trigger notifications:
notifier_dialog.templates_description:
Override default message templates. Leave blank to use defaults.
Placeholders: STOCKPILE_NAME, STOCKPILE_TYPE, SHARD, TIME, ITEM_COUNT,
MATCHED_ITEMS, UNMATCHED_ITEMS, AVG_CONFIDENCE, DURATION, RESOLUTION, ERROR
notifier_dialog.event_required: Please select at least one event to notify.

gui_tab.level_tooltip:
Controls which configuration options are visible in the GUI.

Basic: Essential settings only (recommended for most users)
Advanced: Additional tuning options for power users
Developer: Full access including OCR/Template settings
gui_tab.warning_advanced:
Advanced mode enables additional options that affect scan accuracy.
Only modify these settings if you understand their impact.
gui_tab.warning_developer:
Developer mode enables critical settings including OCR and Template tabs.
Incorrect configuration can completely break scanning functionality.
Only use this if you are a developer or advanced user who understands the risks.
gui_tab.minimize_tooltip:
When enabled, closing the window minimizes to system tray
instead of quitting the application.

The application will continue running in the background.
Right-click the tray icon to access options or quit.
gui_tab.language_tooltip: Select the language for the GUI.

logging_tab.root_level_tooltip:
Global default log level for all loggers.

Messages below this level are filtered out unless
a custom logger overrides it.
logging_tab.log_format_tooltip:
Python logging format string.

Common placeholders:
• %(asctime)s - Timestamp
• %(name)s - Logger name
• %(levelname)s - Log level (DEBUG, INFO, etc.)
• %(message)s - Log message

See Python logging documentation for more options.
logging_tab.date_format_tooltip:
Date/time format for log timestamps.

Uses Python strftime format codes:
• %Y - 4-digit year
• %m - 2-digit month
• %d - 2-digit day
• %H - 24-hour hour
• %M - 2-digit minute
• %S - 2-digit second

Example: %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S produces 2025-01-15 14:30:45
logging_tab.rotate_logs_tooltip:
Automatically rotate log files when they get too large.

When enabled, old logs are archived and new log files are created.
Prevents log files from consuming too much disk space.
logging_tab.log_file_tooltip:
Optional path to save log messages to a file.

If not specified, logs are only written to console.
Useful for debugging and keeping a record of operations.
logging_tab.custom_loggers_tooltip:
Override log levels for specific loggers.

Common loggers:
• uvicorn - Web server logs
• uvicorn.access - HTTP request logs
• foxhole_stockpiles - Application logs

stockpile_types_tab.description:
Add custom aliases for stockpile type names to handle OCR errors.
Enter comma-separated values (e.g., 'seapon, Seapont, 5eaport').
The default translations are already built-in and don't need to be added here.

sav_processing_tab.sav_file_tooltip:
Path to the Foxhole save file (.sav) to process.

This file is typically located at:
Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%/Foxhole/Saved/SaveGames/
WSL: /mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Foxhole/Saved/SaveGames/

Look for files named *_MapData.sav
sav_processing_tab.auto_detect_not_found:
Could not find a Foxhole save file in the default locations.

Please browse to select the file manually.
sav_processing_tab.poll_interval_tooltip:
How often to check for file changes when monitoring.

Lower values detect changes faster but use more CPU.
Recommended: 1.0 seconds.
sav_processing_tab.emit_all_tooltip:
When enabled, outputs all stockpiles on first scan.
When disabled, only outputs changes (useful for monitoring).
sav_processing_tab.emit_all_checkbox: Output all stockpiles on first read
